History of Present Illness:
61-year-old man. One day of right upper abdominal pain, fever and poor appetite. No jaundice, dark urine or pale stools.

Physical Examination:
Right upper-quadrant guarding and focal subcostal tenderness. Temperature 37.7 C; heart rate 94/min; BP 122/74 mmHg; respiratory rate 20/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 12.9 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 227 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 137 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.9 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 54 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 33 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 50 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 44 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 87 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: distended gallbladder with stones, 6 mm hyperemic wall and pericholecystic fluid. Common bile duct 5 mm.
